paper_code_mismatch: The paper's dexterous-manipulation environment (Grasp, a 4-fingered claw hand) and locomotion environment (Fetch) are described in Sec. 4.2.2-4.2.3 but neither grasp.py nor fetch.py appears among the 79 captured files in the current google/brax repo snapshot.
note_gaps: Throughput is reported only qualitatively/order-of-magnitude ('millions', 'hundreds of millions', '~thousands') with no exact numeric axis values surviving parsing from Figs. 2-4; astronaut energy/momentum drift (Fig. 5) is qualitative only, no numeric values; per-environment default timestep/substeps for Ant/Humanoid/Grasp/Fetch are not given (only an illustrative ProtoBuf example with dt=.01, substeps=1).
contact_model: rigid bodies in maximal coordinates; naive/quadratic-scaling pairwise collision detection (no broad-phase acceleration structure); no convex-decomposition or mesh-vs-primitive distinction described
solver: not LCP-based; velocity-level collision updates with Baumgarte stabilization (inspired by the Tiny Differentiable Simulator); joints modeled as spring constraints rather than Featherstone-style articulated-body methods
throughput: millions of simulation steps/sec on a single accelerator (e.g. MuJoCo Ant equivalent on a single chip); scales to hundreds of millions of steps/sec distributed across a 4x2 TPUv3 and other TPU topologies; Ant on a TPUv3 8x8 estimated at ~hundreds of millions of steps/sec vs ~thousands of steps/sec for single-threaded CPU MuJoCo Gym (all figures qualitative/order-of-magnitude, no exact numeric table)
hands_shipped: synthetic 4-fingered claw hand (Grasp environment, non-commercial, from-scratch morphology; not confirmed present in current repo snapshot)
